'''Maurice Ager''' (born [[February 9]],[[ 1984]], in [[Detroit, Michigan]]) was a shooting guard for the [[Michigan State Spartans]] from 2002 until 2006.  The 6-5 guard was best known for his athleticism and pure shooting.  

== 2005 Tournament==
In 2005, Ager lead The Spartans to [[Final Four]] by defeating the [[Kentucky Wildcats]] in a classic double overtime game, in the elite eight.  He was named to the Austin-All Regional team after averaging 16.8 points and 5 boards a game.  Despite putting up 24 points against [[North Carolina]] in the [[Final Four]], the Spartans fell short to the eventual champions.

== Senior Year ==
Even though Ager averaged a team high 19.3 points a game, the Spartans did not live up to the expectations analysts gave them. Once ranked #5 in the country, they received a #6 seed in the NCAA Tournament, where they fell to [[George Mason]] in the first round.(Mason went on to the Final Four)

=== 2005 Maui Invitational Tournament ===
On [[November 22]], 2005 at the [[Maui Invitational Tournament]], Ager faced off against [[Gonzaga]]'s [[Adam Morrison]] in one of the most thrilling battles of the year.  Down 3 with virtually no time remaining on the clock, Ager sunk a trey at the buzzer to send the game into overtime.  Despite finishing with a team high 36 points, Gonzaga knocked of the Spartans in triple overtime 109-106. The next day Ager lead the Spartans with 20 points to defeat Arizona 74 -71,OT.
